scope: All five available Book Two chapters: dialogue repetition, conversational responses, character voice and continuity
status: Second pass reviewed, revised and locally verified
method: Read every chapter in full, follow each exchange in context, compare recurring advice and emotional beats across chapters, then scan normalized complete speech passages for exact repetition. Phrase scanning is supplementary; it does not establish naturalness on its own.

chapters.title: One More Thing to Finish
chapters.assessment: Billy's restrained encouragement and Seth's graduation banter work. Seth's opening one-word answer about finals reads awkwardly beside Billy's question about unfinished work.
chapters.revision: Give Seth a conversational answer about upcoming finals and frustration with the homework. Preserve the weeks of tutoring and his own effort.

chapters.title: Watch Where You Kick
chapters.assessment: Flaming Head's short, concrete instructions suit the training scene. Seth's final spoken lesson restates the instruction and the immediately preceding narrative realization.
chapters.revision: Replace that restatement with an embarrassed request to forget his earlier boast. This recalls the actual accident and keeps the safety realization in the narration.

chapters.title: Room to Breathe
chapters.assessment: The rematch joke, pauses and tentative affection are effective. Seth jumps from Jenny's fear of hurting someone to his wish to impress her without acknowledging the fear. Jenny's polished questions-and-answers analogy resembles the book's other mentor statements.
chapters.revision: Have Seth acknowledge that his drum could also have gone over the edge before admitting he was showing off. Have Jenny respond to his insecurity with her own concrete mistake of not waiting for Flaming Head to finish. Keep the quiet reassurance and imperfect practice.

chapters.title: More to Carry
chapters.assessment: The editor's brief praise is credible and work-focused. The repeated 'got' within the sentence supplies intentional spoken emphasis rather than redundant explanation. Jenny's gratitude is already summarized; another speech would add little.

chapters.title: Words and Actions
chapters.assessment: Larry's words-and-actions advice carries the chapter's central meaning and the photograph preserves the hint about Jenny's identity. His next speech stacks general prescriptions. The clerk and Jenny previously exchange generic statements rather than reacting to the unusual wear.
chapters.revision: Retain Larry's central advice and replace the follow-up maxims with practical questions about what must be done today and what can wait. Give the clerk an ordinary question about the shoes' age and Jenny a rueful answer before she asks for a sturdier pair. Neither exchange confirms her secret.

continuity: No changes to plot, chronology, powers, identities, illustration references or scenes. Seth remains earnest and self-conscious; Jenny's confidence coexists with worry; Billy stays patient; Flaming Head stays direct; Larry's knowledge remains uncertain.
